objective: The selected next step of ROUND-PRICE-20261108-001 (G1, space from a law; A25, A35), started on 2026-11-08 at the coordinator's go-ahead: does one hidden bit per tile force the pinwheel? Sixteen one-bit decorated substitutions (eight up to exchanging the labels) force every parent's label and exclude the three crystal families tested, but pairwise consistency leaves labelled parent collars outside their laws. Settle them: a joint (radius-2) consistency test on the surviving parent collars, which proves that a decoration forces the pinwheel if every off-law survivor dies; then a search for an escaping crystal built from what survives. At the end of the line, a short note for outside readers covers the pinwheel results (no undecorated local rules; the one-bit census). Standalone value against known work: decorated matching rules force the pinwheel with large alphabets (Radin 1994; Goodman-Strauss 1998); whether one bit per tile suffices was not found.
